content: Discs large homolog 1 (DLG1), also referred to as synapse-associated protein 97 (SAP97), is a scaffold protein encoded by the SAP97 gene in humans. It belongs to the mammalian MAGUK (membrane-associated guanylate kinase) family and shares similarities with the Drosophila protein Dlg1. In humans, the protein is also known as hDlg1, and the corresponding gene is named DLG1. SAP97 is widely expressed in epithelial cells throughout the body, including in the kidney and brain. In the brain, it plays a critical role in the trafficking of ionotropic receptors, such as AMPA receptors (AMPAR), from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to the plasma membrane. This trafficking is particularly important during synaptic plasticity. SAP97 has been implicated in regulating cell-to-cell adhesion during processes such as cell death. There is also evidence suggesting that it may interact with human papillomavirus (HPV). In the brain, SAP97 facilitates the movement of transmembrane receptors from the ER to the plasma membrane. Experimental studies have explored its function by either knocking out the SAP97 gene or overexpressing it. Mice with a complete knockout of the SAP97 gene exhibit perinatal lethality, cleft palate formation, and impaired kidney function. Conversely, overexpression of SAP97 in mammalian neurons has been shown to enhance synaptic strength. Mutations in the DLG1 gene have been linked to Crohn's disease, highlighting its clinical significance. The structure of SAP97 is highly modular and consists of several distinct domains, each contributing to its unique functions. These include an alternatively spliced N-terminal domain, three PDZ domains, an SH3 domain, a hook domain, an I3 domain, and an inactive guanylate kinase (GK) domain. The N-terminal domain can undergo alternative splicing to produce either an α-isoform, which contains a double-cysteine/palmitoylation site, or a β-isoform, which includes an L27 domain. The L27 domain facilitates oligomerization of SAP97 with other SAP97 molecules, as well as with proteins like CASK and other L27-domain-containing proteins. Additionally, there is a myosin VI binding site near the N-terminal region, which may play a role in the internalization of AMPA receptors. Each of the three PDZ domains in SAP97 has distinct binding partners. For example, the first PDZ domain interacts with the AMPAR subunit GluR1, while the last PDZ domain binds to neuroligin. The I3 domain is unique to SAP97 among MAGUK family proteins and is involved in regulating the post-synaptic localization of SAP97. It also binds to the protein 4.1N. The GK domain, although catalytically inactive, enables SAP97 to interact with GKAP/SAPAP-family proteins, further contributing to its role in synaptic organization and function.
